questions.question: At the very top of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam family tree, who is shown as the Supreme Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: The chart is headed by KṚṢṆA, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, from whom everything else descends.

questions.question: From whom was Lord Brahmā born?

options.text: Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, an expansion of Kṛṣṇa

questions.explanation: The chart notes Lord Brahmā was 'born from Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, an expansion of Kṛṣṇa.'

questions.question: Marīci, Atri, and Svāyambhuva Manu are all shown descending directly from whom?
questions.explanation: Lord Brahmā is the origin of the three great branches: Marīci, Atri, and Svāyambhuva Manu.

questions.question: Which of these is shown as a son (mind-born son / prajāpati) of Lord Brahmā?
questions.explanation: Alongside Marīci and Atri, Brahmā's sons in the chart include Nārada Muni, the Four Kumāras, Lord Śiva, Kratu, Bhṛgu, Atreya, Pulaha, Vasiṣṭha, Aṅgirā, and Pulastya.

questions.question: Who is shown as the son of Marīci?
questions.explanation: Marīci's son is Kaśyapa, who married Diti, Aditi, and other wives.

questions.question: Diti and Aditi were both wives of which sage?
questions.explanation: Kaśyapa married Diti, Aditi, and other wives.

questions.question: The 49 Maruts, Hiraṇyakaśipu, and Hiraṇyākṣa were the sons of which mother?
questions.explanation: Diti, wife of Kaśyapa, bore the 49 Maruts, Hiraṇyakaśipu, and Hiraṇyākṣa.

questions.question: Vivasvān and many demigods were the sons of which wife of Kaśyapa?
questions.explanation: Aditi, wife of Kaśyapa, bore Vivasvān and many demigods.

questions.question: Who was the wife of Hiraṇyakaśipu?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Hiraṇyakaśipu's wife as Kayādhu.

questions.question: Who was the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu?
questions.explanation: Prahlāda, the great devotee, was the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu.

questions.question: Prahlāda → ? → Bali. Who is the missing link (Prahlāda's son and Bali's father)?
questions.explanation: The line runs Prahlāda → Virocana → Bali.

questions.question: Bali Mahārāja was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Bali (wife: Vindhyāvalī) was the son of Virocana.

questions.question: Who was the wife of Bali Mahārāja?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Bali's wife as Vindhyāvalī.

questions.question: Bāṇa and 99 others were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Bali and Vindhyāvalī had Bāṇa and 99 other sons.

questions.question: Who was the son of Vivasvān and the current Manu?
questions.explanation: Vivasvān's son is Vaivasvata Manu, the current Manu (a.k.a. Śrāddhadeva; wife: Śraddhā).

questions.question: Vaivasvata Manu, the current Manu, is also known as what?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Vaivasvata Manu is the current Manu, a.k.a. Śrāddhadeva (wife: Śraddhā).

questions.question: Which of these was a child of Vaivasvata Manu?
questions.explanation: Vaivasvata Manu's children include Ilā, Nṛga, Ikṣvāku, Śaryāti, Nabhaga, and 6 other sons.

questions.question: Ilā, a child of Vaivasvata Manu, was transformed into whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes 'Ilā (transformed into Sudyumna).'

questions.question: By the churning of whose body was Janaka born, according to the chart?
questions.explanation: The chart notes 'Nimi (by churning, Janaka was born).'

questions.question: Who was the father of Sītā Devī?
questions.explanation: Sītā Devī's father was Śīradhvaja, identified in the chart as 'Janaka, Sītā's father.'

questions.question: Sītā Devī was the wife of whom?
questions.explanation: Sītā Devī (daughter of Śīradhvaja) was the wife of Lord Rāma.

questions.question: Hariścandra, in the Ikṣvāku line, had which son?
questions.explanation: The line runs Hariścandra → Rohita → ... → Sāgara.

questions.question: Which king in the Ikṣvāku line was the father of Aṁśumān?
questions.explanation: The line runs Sāgara → Aṁśumān → Dilīpa → Bhagīratha.

questions.question: Who was the son of Aṁśumān?
questions.explanation: Aṁśumān → Dilīpa → Bhagīratha.

questions.question: Bhagīratha, famous for bringing the Gaṅgā, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart shows Dilīpa → Bhagīratha.

questions.question: Who was the father of Lord Rāmacandra?
questions.explanation: In the chart, Khaṭvāṅga → (some descendants) → Daśaratha, the father of Lord Rāmacandra.

questions.question: Lakṣmaṇa and Lord Rāmacandra were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Daśaratha's sons include Lakṣmaṇa, Lord Rāmacandra, and other sons.

questions.question: Lava and Kuśa were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Lord Rāmacandra (wife: Sītā) had the sons Lava and Kuśa.

questions.question: Sukanyā, who married Cyavana Muni, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Śaryāti's children include Sukanyā (who married Cyavana Muni) and 2 other sons.

questions.question: Sukanyā married which sage?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Sukanyā 'married Cyavana Muni.'

questions.question: The devotee-king Ambarīṣa Mahārāja was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: The line runs Nabhaga → Nābhāga → Ambarīṣa Mahārāja.

questions.question: Nābhāga was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Nabhaga → Nābhāga → Ambarīṣa Mahārāja.

questions.question: Kakudmi's daughter, who married Lord Balarāma, was named what?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Revatī 'married Lord Balarāma.'

questions.question: Revatī, who married Lord Balarāma, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Ānarta → Revata → Kakudmi → Revatī (married Lord Balarāma).

questions.question: In the Ānarta line, who was the father of Kakudmi?
questions.explanation: The line runs Ānarta → Revata → Kakudmi.

questions.question: Who was the son of Atri (in the main descending line)?
questions.explanation: Atri → Soma → Budha (not Lord Buddha) → Purūrava.

questions.question: Budha, the son of Soma, is explicitly distinguished in the chart from whom?
questions.explanation: The chart labels him 'Budha (not Lord Buddha).'

questions.question: Purūrava was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Soma → Budha → Purūrava (wife: Urvaśī).

questions.question: Who was the wife of Purūrava?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Purūrava's wife as Urvaśī.

questions.question: Vijaya and Āyu were among the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Purūrava (wife: Urvaśī) had Vijaya, 4 other sons, and Āyu.

questions.question: Satyavatī and Viśvāmitra were the children of whom?
questions.explanation: In the Vijaya branch, Gadhi's children are Satyavatī and Viśvāmitra (wife: Menakā).

questions.question: According to the chart, who was the wife of Viśvāmitra?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Viśvāmitra's wife as Menakā.

questions.question: Śakuntalā was the daughter of Viśvāmitra and which apsarā?
questions.explanation: Śakuntalā was the daughter of Viśvāmitra (wife: Menakā); her husband was Duṣmanta.

questions.question: Śakuntalā's husband was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Śakuntalā's husband was Duṣmanta (see Puru's descendants).

questions.question: Jamadagni was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Satyavatī → Jamadagni → Lord Paraśurāma.

questions.question: Lord Paraśurāma was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Jamadagni's son was Lord Paraśurāma.

questions.question: Kṣatravṛddha and Nahuṣa were among the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Āyu's sons include Kṣatravṛddha, Nahuṣa, and 3 other sons.

questions.question: Yayāti was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Nahuṣa → Yayāti (and 5 other sons).

questions.question: Yadu and Puru, founders of two great dynasties, were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Yayāti's sons include Yadu, Puru, and 3 other sons.

questions.question: Devayānī, who married Yayāti, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Priyavrata's one daughter married Śukrācārya; their daughter Devayānī married Yayāti.

questions.question: Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka were among the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Sātvata's sons include Vṛṣṇi, Andhaka, and 5 other sons.

questions.question: Śūrasena descended from which son of Sātvata?
questions.explanation: Vṛṣṇi → (many descendants) → Śūrasena.

questions.question: Vasudeva and Kunti were the children of whom?
questions.explanation: Śūrasena's children include Vasudeva, Kunti, and 4 other daughters.

questions.question: Who was the father of Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma?
questions.explanation: Vasudeva's children include Lord Kṛṣṇa, Lord Balarāma, Subhadrā, and 9 other sons.

questions.question: Subhadrā, in the chart, was a daughter (sister of Kṛṣṇa) of whom?
questions.explanation: Subhadrā is listed among Vasudeva's children, alongside Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.

questions.question: Kunti and Vasudeva were siblings; what does this make Kunti to Lord Kṛṣṇa?
questions.explanation: Kunti was Vasudeva's sister (both children of Śūrasena), so she was Kṛṣṇa's paternal aunt.

questions.question: Who was the husband of Kunti?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Kunti's husband as Pāṇḍu.

questions.question: Karṇa and the Pāṇḍavas were born to which mother?
questions.explanation: Kunti (husband: Pāṇḍu) is shown with Karṇa and the Pāṇḍavas.

questions.question: Āhuka descended from which son of Sātvata?
questions.explanation: Andhaka → (many descendants) → Āhuka.

questions.question: Āhuka's two sons were whom?
questions.explanation: Āhuka's sons are Ugrasena and Devaka.

questions.question: Kaṁsa was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Ugrasena's children include Kaṁsa, 5 daughters, and 8 other sons.

questions.question: Devakī, the mother of Kṛṣṇa, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Devaka's children include Devakī, 6 other daughters, and 4 sons.

questions.question: Since Kaṁsa (son of Ugrasena) and Devakī (daughter of Devaka) share a grandfather, who was he?
questions.explanation: Ugrasena and Devaka were both sons of Āhuka, so Kaṁsa and Devakī were his grandchildren.

questions.question: The emperor Bharata (after whom Bhārata is named), son of Duṣmanta, is distinguished in the chart from whom?
questions.explanation: The chart labels him 'Bharata (not Jaḍa Bharata)' in the Puru line.

questions.question: Duṣmanta and Śakuntalā's son was whom?
questions.explanation: In the Puru line, Duṣmanta → Bharata (not Jaḍa Bharata).

questions.question: Rkṣa and Nila were among the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Ajamīḍha's sons include Rkṣa, Nila, and other sons.

questions.question: Kuru, of the Kuru dynasty, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Ajamīḍha → Rkṣa → Kuru → Jāhnu.

questions.question: Who was the son of Kuru?
questions.explanation: Rkṣa → Kuru → Jāhnu → (many descendants).

questions.question: Drupada, father of Draupadī, descended from which son of Ajamīḍha?
questions.explanation: Nila → (many descendants) → Drupada.

questions.question: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Draupadī were the children of whom?
questions.explanation: Drupada's children include Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Draupadī, and other sons.

questions.question: Vicitravīrya, Bhīṣma, and Citrāṅgada were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart shows Śantanu's sons as Vicitravīrya, Bhīṣma, and Citrāṅgada.

questions.question: Bhīṣma was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Bhīṣma is shown as a son of Śantanu.

questions.question: Pāṇḍu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Vidura were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart shows Vicitravīrya → Pāṇḍu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura.

questions.question: Duryodhana, 99 other sons, and 1 daughter were the children of whom?
questions.explanation: Dhṛtarāṣṭra had Duryodhana, 99 other sons, and 1 daughter — 100 sons in all.

questions.question: The five Pāṇḍavas were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: The Pāṇḍavas (Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva) are shown under Pāṇḍu (via Kunti).

questions.question: Which of these is one of the five Pāṇḍavas?
questions.explanation: The five Pāṇḍavas are Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva.

questions.question: Abhimanyu was the son of which Pāṇḍava?
questions.explanation: Arjuna's children are Abhimanyu and 3 other sons.

questions.question: Parīkṣit was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Arjuna → Abhimanyu → Parīkṣit → Janamejaya.

questions.question: Janamejaya was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Parīkṣit's children include Janamejaya and 3 other sons.

questions.question: Following the line Arjuna → Abhimanyu → Parīkṣit → ?, who comes next?
questions.explanation: The line ends with Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit.

questions.question: Who was the wife of Svāyambhuva Manu?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Svāyambhuva Manu's wife as Śatarūpā.

questions.question: Which of these was a son of Svāyambhuva Manu?
questions.explanation: Svāyambhuva Manu's sons were Priyavrata and Uttānapāda; his daughters were Ākūti, Devahūti, and Prasūti.

questions.question: Which of these was a daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu?
questions.explanation: Svāyambhuva Manu's daughters were Ākūti, Devahūti, and Prasūti.

questions.question: How many sons did Priyavrata have (besides 1 daughter)?
questions.explanation: Priyavrata had 1 daughter (who married Śukrācārya) and 13 sons.

questions.question: Of Priyavrata's 13 sons, 3 became sannyāsīs, 3 became Manus, and 7 became what?
questions.explanation: The chart notes 3 became sannyāsīs, 3 became Manus, and 7 became rulers of 7 islands.

questions.question: Āgnīdhra, one of the seven island-rulers, had which wife?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Āgnīdhra's wife as Pūrvacitti.

questions.question: Āgnīdhra had 9 sons who married the 9 daughters of whom?
questions.explanation: Āgnīdhra's 9 sons married the 9 daughters of Meru.

questions.question: The oldest of Āgnīdhra's 9 sons was whom?
questions.explanation: The oldest of the 9 sons is King Nābhi (wife: Merudevī).

questions.question: King Nābhi's wife was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists King Nābhi's wife as Merudevī.

questions.question: Lord Ṛṣabhadeva was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: King Nābhi (wife: Merudevī) → Lord Ṛṣabhadeva (wife: Jayantī).

questions.question: Lord Ṛṣabhadeva's wife was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Lord Ṛṣabhadeva's wife as Jayantī.

questions.question: Bharata, who in his next life became Jaḍa Bharata, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Lord Ṛṣabhadeva (wife: Jayantī) → Bharata (wife: Pañcajanī) [in next life Jaḍa Bharata].

questions.question: This Bharata (son of Ṛṣabhadeva) had which wife?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Bharata's wife as Pañcajanī.

questions.question: Along with Bharata, Lord Ṛṣabhadeva's sons included the '9 Yogendras' and how many other sons?
questions.explanation: Ṛṣabhadeva's sons: Bharata, the 9 Yogendras, and 90 other sons.

questions.question: Mahārāja Gaya descended from which Bharata's line?
questions.explanation: Bharata (son of Ṛṣabhadeva) → many descendants → Mahārāja Gaya.

questions.question: Uttānapāda's two wives were whom?
questions.explanation: Uttānapāda married Suruci and Suniti.

questions.question: Uttama was the son of which wife of Uttānapāda?
questions.explanation: Suruci's son was Uttama; Suniti's son was Dhruva.

questions.question: The great devotee Dhruva was the son of which mother?
questions.explanation: Suniti's son was Dhruva Mahārāja.

questions.question: Uttama and Dhruva were half-brothers, both sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Uttama (via Suruci) and Dhruva (via Suniti) were both sons of Uttānapāda.

questions.question: Dhruva Mahārāja's sons were Vatsara and whom?
questions.explanation: Dhruva's sons were Vatsara (wife: Svarvīthi) and Utkala.

questions.question: Vatsara's wife was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Vatsara's wife as Svarvīthi.

questions.question: Following Dhruva → Vatsara → ? → Vyuṣṭa, who is the missing link?
questions.explanation: The line runs Vatsara → Puṣpārṇa → Vyuṣṭa → Sarvatejā.

questions.question: Who was the son of Vyuṣṭa?
questions.explanation: Vyuṣṭa → Sarvatejā → Cākṣuṣa Manu.

questions.question: Cākṣuṣa Manu, in the Dhruva line, is identified as which Manu?
questions.explanation: The chart labels Cākṣuṣa Manu as the Sixth Manu.

questions.question: Cākṣuṣa Manu was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Sarvatejā → Cākṣuṣa Manu → Ulmuka.

questions.question: Ulmuka, son of Cākṣuṣa Manu, had which son?
questions.explanation: Cākṣuṣa Manu → Ulmuka → Aṅga → Vena.

questions.question: Aṅga's wife, the daughter of Death, was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Aṅga's wife as Sunīthā, daughter of Death.

questions.question: The infamous King Vena was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Aṅga (wife: Sunīthā) → Vena.

questions.question: From the churning of King Vena's thighs came which sinful race?
questions.explanation: From churning Vena's thighs came Niṣāda (the sinful race).

questions.question: Mahārāja Pṛthu was produced from the churning of which part of King Vena?
questions.explanation: From churning Vena's right hand came Pṛthu (wife: Arci).

questions.question: Who was the wife of Mahārāja Pṛthu?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Pṛthu's wife as Arci.

questions.question: Vijitāśva, son of Pṛthu, was also known by which name?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Vijitāśva 'a.k.a. Antardhāna.'

questions.question: Vijitāśva (Antardhāna) was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Pṛthu → Vijitāśva (a.k.a. Antardhāna) → Havirdhāna.

questions.question: Who was the son of Vijitāśva (Antardhāna)?
questions.explanation: Vijitāśva → Havirdhāna → Barhiṣat.

questions.question: Barhiṣat, son of Havirdhāna, was also known by all of these names EXCEPT which?
questions.explanation: Barhiṣat is a.k.a. Prajāpati, Prācīnabarhi, and Barhiṣmān. 'Antardhāna' was the other name of Vijitāśva.

questions.question: The ten Pracetās were the sons of whom?
questions.explanation: Barhiṣat → the Pracetās (10 sons; wife: Māriṣā).

questions.question: The Pracetās' wife was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists the Pracetās' wife as Māriṣā.

questions.question: Dakṣa (in the Dhruva/Pṛthu line) was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: The Pracetās → Dakṣa (wife: Asiknī).

questions.question: This Dakṣa's wife was whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Dakṣa's wife as Asiknī.

questions.question: Dakṣa's 60 daughters are noted as having done what?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Dakṣa's 60 daughters 'created many species.'

questions.question: Dakṣa's 10,000 Haryaśvas and 10,000 Savalaśvas both became what?
questions.explanation: Both the Haryaśvas and Savalaśvas are noted as sannyāsīs.

questions.question: This Dakṣa is noted as being Prasūti's husband in which context?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Dakṣa was 'Prasūti's husband in his next life.'

questions.question: Who was the husband of Ākūti (daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu)?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Ākūti's husband as Ruci.

questions.question: Yajña, an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Ākūti (husband: Ruci) had Yajña, an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, and Dakṣiṇa.

questions.question: Who was the husband of Prasūti (daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu)?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Prasūti's husband as Dakṣa.

questions.question: Satī, the wife of Lord Śiva, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Satī (wife of Lord Śiva) is shown as a daughter of Dakṣa and Prasūti.

questions.question: Satī married which deity?
questions.explanation: Satī is labeled 'wife of Lord Śiva.'

questions.question: Aditi and Diti, who married Kaśyapa, are shown as daughters of which couple?
questions.explanation: Aditi (husband: Kaśyapa) and Diti (husband: Kaśyapa) are daughters of Dakṣa and Prasūti — the reason their descendants 'continue on the left, under Marīci.'

questions.question: Mūrti, a daughter of Dakṣa and Prasūti, married whom?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Mūrti's husband as Dharma.

questions.question: Nara-Nārāyaṇa, the combined form of Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, was the son of Mūrti and whom?
questions.explanation: Mūrti (husband: Dharma) → Nara-Nārāyaṇa (form of Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna).

questions.question: Nara-Nārāyaṇa is noted in the chart as having created Apsarās like whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Nara-Nārāyaṇa 'created Apsarās like Urvaśī.'

questions.question: Who was the husband of Devahūti?
questions.explanation: The chart lists Devahūti's husband as Kardama (Muni).

questions.question: Lord Kapila, the incarnation who taught Sāṅkhya to His mother, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: Lord Kapila is shown as the son of Kardama and Devahūti.

questions.question: Kalā, who married Marīci, was a daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Kalā (husband: Marīci) is a daughter of Devahūti and Kardama.

questions.question: Kalā and Marīci's sons were Kaśyapa and whom?
questions.explanation: Kalā (husband: Marīci) had Kaśyapa and Pūrṇimā.

questions.question: According to the chart, who were the parents of Kaśyapa?
questions.explanation: Kaśyapa is Marīci's son via Kalā (a daughter of Devahūti) — closing a loop in the tree.

questions.question: Anasūyā, who married Atri, was a daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Anasūyā (husband: Atri) is a daughter of Devahūti and Kardama.

questions.question: Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā were the sons of Atri and which wife?
questions.explanation: Anasūyā (husband: Atri) → Soma, Dattātreya, Durvāsā.

questions.question: Soma (son of Atri and Anasūyā) was a partial incarnation of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Soma was a 'partial incarnation of Brahmā.'

questions.question: Dattātreya was a partial incarnation of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Dattātreya was a 'partial incarnation of Viṣṇu.'

questions.question: Durvāsā, famous for his temper, was a partial incarnation of whom?
questions.explanation: The chart notes Durvāsā was a 'partial incarnation of Śiva.'

questions.question: Dattātreya and Durvāsā were both sons of which sage?
questions.explanation: Atri (via Anasūyā) had Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā.

questions.question: The three great original branches of the family tree stem from Brahmā's sons Marīci, Atri, and whom?
questions.explanation: The tree's three main branches are Marīci (→ Kaśyapa), Atri (→ Soma), and Svāyambhuva Manu.

questions.question: Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma appear in the chart within which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma descend from Yadu → Sātvata → Vṛṣṇi → Śūrasena → Vasudeva.

questions.question: The Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas (Mahābhārata) belong to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Puru → Bharata → ... → Kuru → Śantanu → the Pāṇḍavas and Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons.

questions.question: Lord Rāmacandra belongs to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Rāma descends from Vaivasvata Manu → Ikṣvāku → ... → Daśaratha → Lord Rāmacandra.

questions.question: Which chain of incarnations were the three sons of Atri and Anasūyā?
questions.explanation: Atri and Anasūyā's sons — Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā — were partial incarnations of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva respectively.
